item.title: Self-Hosted Building Energy Modeling: EnergyPlus vs OpenStudio vs Modelica Buildings
item.description:
Introduction

Building energy modeling (BEM) is the computational simulation of a building’s energy use, thermal loads, and environmental performance. Architects, engineers, and sustainability consultants use BEM tools to predict heating and cooling demands, optimize HVAC systems, evaluate daylighting strategies, and demonstrate code compliance for green building certifications like LEED and BREEAM. With building operations accounting for roughly 30% of global energy consumption, accurate energy modeling has never been more important.

item.title: Self-Hosted Energy System Modeling Frameworks: PyPSA vs Calliope vs OpenModelica
item.description:
Why Self-Host Energy System Modeling?

The global energy transition demands sophisticated tools to model increasingly complex electricity systems. Grid operators, energy consultancies, and academic research groups need to simulate scenarios integrating renewables, storage, demand response, and sector coupling — from rooftop solar adoption rates to continent-scale transmission expansion. Commercial tools like PLEXOS and Aurora command five-figure annual licenses per seat, putting them out of reach for municipal planning agencies and university departments.
